text: Everything you've written so far has run on a simulator on your own machine. To submit a job to real hardware, a resource-estimator target, or even a cloud simulator, you first need an Azure Quantum workspace — an Azure resource that acts as the front door between your Q# code and every provider Azure Quantum connects you to.

An Azure Quantum workspace isn't a separate quantum-specific cloud — it's an ordinary Azure resource, provisioned inside a resource group, inside your subscription, exactly the way a storage account is. It shows up in the Portal's resource list, bills through the same subscription, and is governed by the same RBAC roles your organization already uses. Two things it specifically needs: a linked storage account to hold job inputs and outputs, and at least one provider added — and providers aren't workspace-wide defaults, each workspace explicitly lists which ones it can access.

The Portal flow works for a first workspace, but scripting it with the Azure CLI's quantum extension is the more realistic path once you're managing workspaces repeatably. You create a resource group, then create the workspace itself, pointing at a linked storage account. The provider-sku-list argument is where you declare which providers and plan tiers this workspace gets access to — you can add more to an existing workspace later without recreating it.

Once a workspace exists, your code needs its identity to submit jobs. From Python, the azure-quantum package's Workspace object takes the subscription ID, resource group, workspace name, and location directly — or a single connection string copied from the Portal's overview page. Authentication happens through your existing Azure credentials, an az login session or a managed identity in a pipeline — you're not managing separate Azure Quantum API keys.

Next lesson sorts out exactly what you can point that workspace at — simulators, the resource estimator, and real hardware are three genuinely different things, and picking the wrong one for where you are wastes either time or real money.
